# Appeal of Denial – Bunion Surgery (CPT 28296)

**RE: Request for Reconsideration of Adverse Benefit Determination**
Member: Quinn Jennings
Member ID: W670697505
Reference number: POC-6E16FAD700-45453
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-04
Plan: Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Georgia
Procedure: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296

This letter is governed by **Aetna CPB 0629 - Bunionectomy** (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0629.html), last review 12/11/2025.

Dear Aetna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my bunion surgery, referenced above. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me, and I believe the records already submitted show that I meet Aetna's own published criteria for this surgery. I am asking that this denial be reconsidered.

## How my records match Aetna's own criteria

Aetna's policy states that it "considers the following interventions medically necessary" for "[m]embers with clinical symptoms and a history of conservative management who meet the following criteria," including:

> "Bony Correction Bunionectomy Bony correction bunionectomy (e.g., Akin, Chevron, Keller, Lapidus, Mitchell, proximal metatarsal osteotomy procedures, etc.) to treat symptomatic hallux valgus (bunion) in a skeletally mature individual (i.e., after epiphyseal closure) or an individual who is 18 years of age or older when the following criteria is met:"

and

> "The member's pain and symptoms over the medial bony eminence or calluses persist, making walking difficult despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional that includes the following:"

My records show:

- **Skeletal maturity / age:** [Please insert or confirm my date of birth/age on file, as this was not restated in the denial notice.]
- **Persistent pain making walking difficult:** I have had 24 months of progressive pain in my foot, unrelieved by rest, and I cannot tolerate closed shoes because of the risk of ulceration over the bony prominence.
- **Conservative treatment under a healthcare professional's direction, at least 6 months:** I completed NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-25 (giving only 4 weeks of partial relief), and 10 weeks (18 visits, 2026-04-12 through 2026-06-21) of physical therapy including activity modification and a custom orthotic, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.

Aetna's policy separately lists specific conservative measures, including:

> "Corticosteroid injections;"

which I have documented above, and:

> "Shoe inserts (generally contractually excluded);"

which is reflected by the custom orthotic I was fitted with.

The policy also lists:

> "Protective cushions/pads;"

and

> "Debridement of hyperkeratotic lesions;"

My submitted records do not specifically mention these two measures. If my chart from Dr. Duval's office contains additional documentation on these points, I am asking that it be requested and reviewed before a final decision is made, since the denial reason given was "incomplete documentation" rather than a finding that I do not meet the clinical criteria.

## Findings that do not appear to apply to my request

Aetna's policy also discusses arthrodesis (fusion) and advanced disease, including:

> "Fusion is the procedure of choice for hallux valgus associated with advanced degenerative joint disease, and advanced hallux valgus (IMA greater than 20 degrees, HVA greater than 40 degrees), severely subluxated or dislocated MTP joints, or for failed hallux valgus surgery."

My weight-bearing radiographs from 2026-06-29 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees. Because my procedure requested, CPT 28296, is a bony correction bunionectomy and not an arthrodesis/fusion procedure, I do not believe the arthrodesis-specific criteria below are the ones that should be applied to my case:

> "Another indication for arthrodesis includes a failed Keller bunionectomy."

> "Arthrodesis or a Keller procedure is the generally accepted treatment of choice following failed cheilectomy or where advanced degenerative changes are present."

I have not had a prior Keller bunionectomy or cheilectomy, so these provisions do not appear to describe my situation.

The policy also states:

> "Minimum follow-up was at least 12 months."

I am not certain how this applies to a prior-authorization decision rather than to outcomes data in a clinical study. I would appreciate clarification of how this specific line was applied to my request, since my records do not show that this was explained as a reason for denial beyond the general statement of "incomplete documentation."

Finally, the policy states that:

> "According to accepted guidelines, treatment should initially consist of conservative measures;"

As described above, I have already completed a course of conservative measures, including medication, injection, physical therapy, and bracing/orthotic support, over a period of months, without lasting relief.

## Request

Based on the above, I am asking Aetna to reconsider this denial and to approve coverage for CPT 28296, or to specify exactly what additional documentation is needed from Dr. Duval's office to complete the medical necessity review. I understand this letter does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-01-31** (180 days from the date of the denial notice, 2026-08-04). I will submit this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, and will fax it to 859-425-3379 (I will also confirm the correct appeal address printed on my denial notice before sending). I can also be reached at 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my member card if additional information is needed.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Quinn Jennings
Member ID: W670697505
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [date of signing]

Enclosures: [Physical therapy discharge note; radiology report dated 2026-06-29; medication and injection records; surgeon's letter of medical necessity, if available]
